specs.value: Porous clay gravel substrate, specially fractured, for planted aquariums
Natural mineral ore; no coating or chemical treatment
Lasts as long as the aquarium; never needs replacing (Seachem). Vietnamese shops say at least 3 years.
Stays intact when wet; does not soften or break down
Part of the same range on Seachem's site; sold in Vietnam
Separate product in the same range; do not mix it up with Flourite Black

fits.fact: Made mainly for planted tanks, but works in any freshwater aquarium
Works best as the only substrate, but can be mixed with other gravel; no laterite needed
Can be used with an under-gravel filter
The shop says it is shrimp-safe
Can hold shrimp but is not optimised for them; a substrate made for shrimp may be better
Flourite Black is suggested for Bucephalandra, aroids and ferns
Because it does not change pH, it suits low-tech tanks where you don't want to soften the water

usage.fact: It comes pre-washed but can get dusty in transit, so rinse it before use (shops say 1–2 times)
Fill the tank slowly by pouring water into a bowl set on the substrate
Cloudy water at first is normal. Use filter floss and, if you like, Seachem Clarity to clear it faster
Water usually clears in about 2–12 hours, depending on the filter
To estimate how much you need: tank length (cm) × width (cm) ÷ 180 = kg. Example: a 100×40 cm tank needs about 22 kg
To add it to a running tank, add small rinsed batches 12–24 hours apart; fine particles may clog mechanical filter media
No need to replace it when nutrients run out; add liquid fertiliser or root tabs instead. Flourish, Flourish Tabs and Flourish Iron are optional add-ons

issues.fact: Hobbyists report heavy cloudiness and dust when setting up, and cloudiness again when gravel-vacuuming hard
Independent reviews say it does not feed plants on its own, so root feeders need root tabs. This contradicts shop claims that it supplies nutrients
Because it is crushed stone, it releases only limited nutrients
Prices vary widely between shops: the 3.5 kg bag ranges from 290,000 to 380,000 VND
The Greendeal listing contradicts itself on the colour of the original Flourite (dark grey/black vs dark red)
The Black version costs more than the original at the same shop: 430,000 vs 380,000 VND for 3.5 kg

alternatives.why: A cheaper aqua soil (about 280,000 VND) made for low-tech planted tanks. Unlike Flourite, it is a nutrient soil, but it breaks down over time
A premium, nutrient-rich soil that lowers pH; better for demanding stem plants and shrimp, but costs more and has a shorter life than Flourite
A cheaper, inert porous clay substrate with a similar long-lasting, non-decomposing role; needs root tabs too
